candidates.title: Stucked Hover in streamlit-bokeh charts
candidates.text:
### Summary

When using Bokeh charts embedded in Streamlit, an issue occurs during page rerendering (triggered by widget interaction, page reload, or Streamlit state updates). If the cursor is hovering over a chart data point while the rerender is in progress and a Bokeh hover tooltip is visible, the tooltip remains rendered on the screen after the rerender completes.

The hover overlay becomes detached from the chart lifecycle and persists across page transitions. The artifact remains visible even when navigating to different Streamlit pages.

The issue disappears only after performing a full browser hard refresh (Ctrl + F5 / Ctrl + Shift + R).

## **Version 1.60.0**

_Release date: July 21, 2026_

**Highlights**

- ✨ You can now disable bulk data export app-wide with the new `client.disableDataExport` config option. When set, the CSV export button is hidden for [`st.dataframe`](/develop/api-reference/data/st.dataframe), [`st.data_editor`](/develop/api-reference/data/st.data_editor), and chart table views, and clipboard copy is disabled for read-only dataframes ([#15910](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15910), [#8402](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8402), [#11358](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11358)).

**Notable Changes**

candidates.title: Disable st.data_editor by cell (and row): cell/row-level editability
candidates.text:
### Summary

**Current Behavior**: Only full columns of an `st.data_editor` can be enabled or disabled for user-editing.

**Feature Request**: Allow for assigning editability on cell (and row) level. For example, an editable column should be disabled for cells (rows) where a certain condition is met.

**Workaround**: Currently, there is no functional workaround. I tried to implement a customized handling of the user input to catch undesired edits and raise an exception when a user edits a cell that should not be editable (in a non-disabled column). However the session_state (e.g. `st.session_state[<data_editor_key>]["edited_rows"].items()`)of the `st.data_editor` does not allow for manipulating the user-input, so the user has to manually undo their changes or refresh the streamlit page and (potentially) re-enter all other edits (in case of bulk edits).

candidates.title: A custom component cannot own the `r` or `c` keys: the app-level shortcuts fire regardless
candidates.text:
### Current Behavior

The capture-phase listener above receives the event, and the app reruns anyway.

Measured on **Streamlit 1.61.1**, driving a real browser and checking whether the app acted:

| focused element | `r` | `c` |
|---|---|---|
| page body | app acts | app acts |
| `<div tabindex="0">` | **app acts** | **app acts** |
| `<button>` | app acts | app acts |
| `<input type="text">` | — | — |
| `<textarea>` | — | — |
| `<select>` | — | — |
| `contenteditable` region | — | — |

So the exemption is by element type. Anything a component builds that is not one of those four native types is subject to the shortcuts, including the focusable containers that keyboard-driven widgets normally use.

<kbd>Esc</kbd> behaves differently and is **not** part of this report: it acts only while one of Streamlit's own overlays is open, which is ordinary dismiss behaviour.

candidates.title: Altair/Vega-Lite native toolbar: hover the download icon to choose PNG or SVG
candidates.text:
### Why?

I'm always frustrated when I hover an Altair/Vega-Lite chart, see the native download icon beside Fullscreen, click it, and can only get PNG.

For reports and papers I often need SVG (vector, scalable) as well as PNG. The old Vega-Embed ⋯ menu offered "Save as PNG" / "Save as SVG". After https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15806, that menu is gone, SVG export is gone, and `usermeta.embedOptions` can no longer restore export actions.

Workarounds (custom HTML components, extra `st.download_button`s, or DOM hacks) either leave the native toolbar unused or drift out of style as Streamlit's toolbar design changes. There is no public API to attach a format menu to the existing toolbar download button.

Related but different: #8177 is about PNG resolution, not choosing a format.

candidates.title: Enhance menu button with download payload capability
candidates.text:
### How?

Ship either a **new widget** (for example `st.download_menu_button`) or an **extension** of `st.menu_button` / `st.download_button` so one control can:
1. Show a dropdown of export labels.
2. On selection, trigger a download using the **payload mapped to that label**.
**Options API (sketch for discussion)**
Accept a structured mapping instead of plain string labels only, for example:
- A **list of tuples or small dicts**, e.g. `(label, file_name, mime, data)`; or  
- A **dict** keyed by label with values like `{ "data": ..., "file_name": ..., "mime": ... }`.
**Lazy payloads**
Allow `data` (or the equivalent field) to be a **callable** that Streamlit invokes **only when that option is chosen**, so expensive exports are not built on every rerun. Document when the callable runs, error handling, and any constraints (e.g. serialization, size limits).

candidates.title: Add a command menu / command palette widget (CMD+K)
candidates.text:
### How?

A widget that registers a searchable list of commands and opens as an overlay on `Cmd/Ctrl+K` (and/or programmatically). Rough sketch:

```python
choice = st.command_menu(
    [
        {"label": "Go to Dashboard", "icon": ":material/dashboard:", "group": "Navigation"},
        {"label": "Export data", "icon": ":material/download:", "group": "Actions"},
    ],
    placeholder="Type a command or search...",
)
if choice == "Export data":
    ...
```

Possible features:
- Fuzzy search, grouping/sections, icons, keyboard navigation.
- Customizable trigger shortcut and a programmatic open.
- Returns the selected command (rerun-based), similar to other widgets.
- Optionally integrate with multipage navigation (pages appear as commands automatically).

candidates.title: Altair/Vega-Lite native toolbar: hover the download icon to choose PNG or SVG
candidates.section: Altair/Vega-Lite native toolbar: hover the download icon to choose PNG or SVG > How?
candidates.text:
### How?

Keep the existing native download icon on Altair/Vega-Lite (and other Vega) charts, in the same toolbar row as Fullscreen.

When the pointer hovers that download icon, show a compact dropdown that matches the toolbar (same icon size, radius, colors, light/dark theme). Suggested items:

- Download PNG
- Download SVG

Clicking an item exports from the current Vega view (`toImageURL("png")` / `toImageURL("svg")`) and starts a browser download.

A click with no menu selection can keep today's PNG-only behavior as the default.

I do not need a new `st` command. Optional later: `st.altair_chart(..., download_formats=("png", "svg"))` to choose which items appear. A Python API is nice-to-have; the hover menu on the native icon is the main request.

Please do not bring back the old Vega-Embed ⋯ menu (View Source / Open in Vega Editor). This should stay a Streamlit toolbar control.

candidates.title: Option to set the chart background to something else than the primary background
candidates.section: Option to set the chart background to something else than the primary background > Problem
candidates.text:
### Problem

As of streamlit 1.16 the chart background color has been changed to match the primary color. This can is some cases make graphs difficult to read. Hence I would like an option to set the chart background separately for all pages in a multipage app. 

I have tried to use
```
import plotly.io as pio
pio.templates.default = "none" 
```
I have also tried to add "plot_bgcolor="grey" to the streamlit theme.

But to no avail, the background color stays the same as the primary color.

I can of cause set theme=None in each st.plotly_chart(), but as my app is large this is cumbersome, and will make it difficult to go back to the streamlit theme. 

My suggestion is therefore twofold.
Make a global option for setting the graph theme, either in the config.toml or on the main page.

Add an option to set the graph background color in config.toml like:
`chartBackgroundColer="#F0F2F6" `
or 
`chartBackgroundColer=secondaryBackgroundColor`

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

Best regards Kristian
